issues.failure_explanation: The displayed MSTD statistic divides the norm of the sample standard deviation by N_s. A standard deviation over N_s samples already averages over those samples, so the extra factor 1/N_s makes the quantity a scaled statistic, not the mean standard deviation named in the text.

failure_location.quote: mean standard deviation (MSTD) that are defined by

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the extra /N_s from the MSTD definition, or rename the statistic as a scaled RMS/std quantity and annotate all reported MSTD values accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: All reported MSTD values and their interpretation as mean sample standard deviations are unreliable; the uncertainty metric in the tables is not the advertised MSTD.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition added-2 only proves an entropy equality for a specific identity-covariance Gaussian chain. It does not prove that the stochastic learned DDPM transition is the deterministic optimal transport map between N(m,I) and N(0,I); no OT map is constructed or shown to be recovered by the training objective.

failure_location.quote: which indeed corresponds to the optimal transport map between the two Gaussians

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the sentence or replace it with a qualified statement that an OT interpretation requires an additional argument not present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The OT interpretation is an unsupported theoretical claim; it overstates what the entropy proposition establishes and may mislead readers about the nature of the learned diffusion model.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that DDPM learns the optimal transport map
issues.why_classification: The defect is a single overreaching interpretive sentence; removing or qualifying it does not alter the method, VLB derivation, or empirical results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Gaussian distribution with the identity covariance
corrupting the output $u$ by an additive Gaussian noise

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition added-2 assumes the initial state u_0 is a Gaussian random vector with identity covariance (and a fixed mean). In the operator-learning noisy setting, u_0|a is Gaussian with a-dependent covariance Sigma(a), and the marginal over a is generally a mixture; the source does not establish the identity-covariance hypothesis for the diffusion input. Therefore the claimed optimality of Sigma_theta = beta_t I for general additive Gaussian noise is outside the proposition's hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: in the Gaussian noise setting is optimal

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit conditional identity-covariance standardization assumption under which the claim holds, or derive the correct reverse covariance for u_0|a ~ N(m(a), Sigma(a)) and state the limitations of beta_t I; otherwise withdraw the optimality claim.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification for the Gaussian-noise reverse covariance choice and for the associated noise-magnitude/uncertainty optimality is unsupported for the general experiments; the beta_t I choice becomes an unproved heuristic.
issues.title: Gaussian-noise covariance optimality misapplies Proposition added-2
issues.why_classification: A local deletion would lose the advertised optimality guarantee, but preserving it requires either a new assumption not satisfied by several tests or a nontrivial covariance correction; the algorithm and empirical results can survive as a heuristic, so this is more than minor but not a full architectural failure.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: maximizing the usual variational lower bound (VLB)
In both cases, the noise-free and Gaussian noise

issues.failure_explanation: The training objective is a VLB optimized by stochastic gradient descent; it does not imply equality between the learned reverse chain and the true reverse chain. The displayed entropy equality requires q_theta to reproduce the true reverse chain in the relevant sense, which is not established for the learned finite network. Moreover, the statement equates self-entropies E_q[-log q] and E_p[-log p], not the likelihood term E_p[-log q] that must match E_p[-log p] for the VLB to be tight. In the conditional setting it also omits conditioning on a.

failure_location.quote: achieves the exact likelihood under the true model

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the statement to hold only in the ideal case where q_theta reproduces the true forward/reverse joint (or delete it), while retaining the VLB as a lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that PDNO attains the true likelihood in both noise-free and Gaussian-noise settings is false as written; any guarantee of exact likelihood or tight VLB based on that sentence is unreliable.
issues.title: Claim that learned q_theta achieves exact likelihood is unsupported
issues.why_classification: The claim is a central theoretical overstatement, but the method's actual objective and empirical claims can survive if the exact-likelihood sentence is weakened to the standard tightness condition; no new proof architecture is needed to state the corrected limitation.
